notes.title: Update 1.1.0
notes.content:
[h1]NEW & IMPROVEMENTS[/h1]
[list]
[*]Added Russian localization.
[*]Added an option to play on a resizable window (only available in main menu).
[*]Added Buttons in game under the Season Dial to speed up(x2), slow down (x0.5) or stop time.
[*]Added a game tool to enable or disable manual fire, to prevent undesired fires on click.
[*]Added a game tool to control clouds opacity to improve visibility with a thick layer of clouds, fog and smoke.
[*]Added a game setting to select terrain size. 
[b]⚠WARNING⚠[/b] While playing on smaller terrain can improve performances, playing on bigger terrains could have a noticeable impact on your performances on lower configurations.
[*]Added world weather stats displaying clouds cover (average humidity) and world temperature.
[*]Added a new tool to replace any plant with a plant of your choice: The Tile Painter.
[*]Added a shortcut (F1) to open the Encyclopedia in game.
[*]Added an access to Credits in the main menu.
[/list]

[h1]FIXES[/h1]
[*]Fixed Pause Menu not opening on game menu screen if closed on another screen.
[*]Fixed an issue where clicking on buttons would prevent camera movement.
[*]Fixed an issue where the cursor would remain hidden in the Pause Menu if HUD was hidden.

notes.title: FireStarter 2 is out!
notes.content:
[h1]FireStarter 2 is out![/h1]

[h2]Why FireStarter 2?[/h2]

Three years ago, I released [url=https://shodanel.itch.io/firestarter]FireStarter[/url], a small and simple forest fire simulation game with little to no ambition, made with a friend of mine during a  week-long game jam.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45092626/777c1b19c3aab3451607ca55915d4707cfa713dd.png[/img]

As the game was appreciated by our players, I wanted to offer more. Wildfires are getting more and more concerning as Climate change rages on and too few people care about that until they are directly concerned. [b]About 9 out 10 wildfire is of human cause[/b]. We're all responsible

This is why I bring to you [b]FireStarter 2[/b], a simplified forest fire simulation game in which all features of FireStarter have been reworked and improved for a [b]more realistic weather and fire behavior[/b] and a much better experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45092626/bd635ea1f9ad1445ab72c4083e48e72818fbb47d.png[/img]

[h2]What to Expect?[/h2]
In FireStarter 2, an [b]autonomous weather and seasonal cycle[/b] can now simulate natural fires and plant growth on its own. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45092626/a0965a6ea01bdfaa80f468626b188f81fbd4eab0.jpg[/img]

You can chose to stay back and observe or play with the many tools in your hands to influence nature development and shape the landscape, such as wind speed and direction control, cloud creation, or even starting your own fires out of nowhere.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45092626/845bb89839f9ed77ce609913e668ff13975b81de.jpg[/img]

A game session should last [b]about 15 minutes[/b], from burning an entire forest to getting it to grow back again, but the game cycle itself is [b]endless [/b]and you're to burn again and again and watch nature fight back again and again.

Of course, I am doing prevention and education here and I strongly believe that this kind of resource should be [b]free [/b]and accessible to everyone, and so is FireStarter 2!

I hope you'll enjoy FireStarter 2 as much as I loved creating it.
